# Time Series and Trends

## Time Series

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Time on the *x* axis, a measurement on the *y* axis
- Connecting dots with lines shows order and trend
- The lines are a guide to the eye, not data
- Slopegraph: a few cases over a few time points
- Slope shows the size and direction of change
- Example: CO~2~ emissions per person, 2000--2010

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-co2-slopegraph-three-year", fig_co2_slopegraph_three_year(),
          w = 4.5, h = 4.5, x = 9, y = 1.2, width = 6.3)
```

## Individual time series

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Time on the *x* axis, a measurement on the *y* axis
- Connecting dots with lines shows order and trend
- The lines are a guide to the eye, not data
- Example: monthly bioRxiv preprint submissions

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-biorxiv-dots-line", fig_biorxiv_dots_line(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Line and area plots

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Shading under the line emphasizes the magnitude, not just the trend
- Area plot appropriate when the *y* axis starts at zero
- Removing dots and adding area shading highlights overall trend relative to points

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-biorxiv-line-area", fig_biorxiv_line_area(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Multiple time series

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Dots with a legend: hard to match colors and shapes to series
- Direct labels at line ends are easier to read
- Lines make each series' trend clear
- Order labels to match line ends

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-bio-preprints-dots", fig_bio_preprints_dots(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 9.5, y = 1.6, width = 4.2)
place_fig("fig-bio-preprints-direct-label", fig_bio_preprints_direct_label(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 9.5, y = 5.0, width = 4.2)
```

## Dose--response curves

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- The same line-plot approach works when *x* is not time
- *x* = treatment level (manure), *y* = mean response (oat yield)
- One line per group (variety) makes comparisons easy
- Use distinct colors and shapes for each group

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-oats-yield", fig_oats_yield(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Moving averages

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Smooth noisy time series by averaging over a window
- Window length sets the scale of fluctuations that remain
- Trailing average (top) lags the data; centered average (bottom) does not
- Limits: shorter than the original series, and still wiggly

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-dow-jones-moving-ave", fig_dow_jones_moving_ave(),
          w = 6.5, h = 6.5, x = 8.5, y = 1.2, width = 7)
```

## Smoothers

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- LOESS and GAMs fit smooth curves to scatter data
- Panel a is LOESS; panels b--d use different GAM settings
- Results depend heavily on the smoother and its parameters
- Try several choices before trusting a trend

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-tank-capacity-smoothers", fig_tank_capacity_smoothers(),
          w = 7.5, h = 5.6, x = 8, y = 1.5, width = 7.8)
```
